message.content:
**Attack.** Gemini’s switch rule is not a measurement fix. Quote: “switch the operational model to Curve_BEY unless Δ skill_OF(BEY − disc) < −0.50 pp.” Skill here is relative log-loss in percentage points. Base-rate log-loss is 0.442 nats, so −0.50 pp is 0.0022 nats. The oracle-censored paired interval is already [−0.042, +0.239] nats on 9 blocks; 0.002 nats is ~0.03 of that half-width. The gate fails only in a catastrophe and otherwise rubber-stamps a switch. The error is not a constant: BEY − d is 0.10 pp at 4%, 0.55–0.81 pp at 12–15%, and 4 of 12 onsets sit in that window. A skill gate set after seeing that pattern selects the correction on the same onsets it reweights. §1.3 is not satisfied by promising a later replay of a rule that has already chosen the winner.

Opus’s bound is the same move in smaller type. Quote: “|Δ oracle-free walk-forward| < 2 pp and |Δβ| < 0.15 per pp.” |β| is 1.29 per pp. At the Volcker onsets the discount curve is 0.55–0.81 pp too high (inversions shallower than BEY), against inversion scales of order 1–3 pp — 20–50% of the regressor at the onsets with the most leverage. A 0.15 cap on Δβ is 12% of |β| and is not implied by that error. His defense of C6 — other warnings already argue against P, so this one may too — treats an existing leak as a precedent. The firewall is a prohibition, not a quota.

GPT’s hold on C7 is a misread. Quote: “F5/curve-only labels reverse the attribution.” 27.05 − 23.16 = 3.89; “F5 +23.2% vs curve-only +27.1%” is 27.1 − 23.2 = 3.9, same sign. Not reversed. The defect is reprinting +27.1.

**Steelman.** Fable’s Jensen point, which I missed. BEY(d) = 365d/(360 − 0.91d) is convex in d, so BEY of a monthly-average discount rate is not the average of daily BEYs. The live input is a trailing mean of daily bills. Part A must convert each DTB3 day, then average, and print the 1954–2026 gap between that and converting TB3MS once. Otherwise the sensitivity compares two different operators.

**Revised positions.**

Q1. Still seal as an unscored diagnostic only. Convert both; no GS3M splice; GS3M is a check. Adopt mean-of-converted for daily DTB3, disclose convexity, print the monthly-average bias. Keep the rate-bin table (0–4, 4–8, 8–12, >12) with onset counts. No automatic switch, no −0.50 pp gate, no |Δ| ≥ 2 pp convening trigger, no |Δβ| < 0.15. Those sentences, if anyone keeps them, are labelled “author’s prior, not a criterion” and are not printed next to the result. Item (4) stays off the dashboard and out of LOG.md. Call the series a 91-day BEY proxy, not CMT.

Q2. Unchanged on the decision: B1/B2 struck, not parked. Closure text must say, verbatim, that E3’s −77.88 pp and 0% positive folds rejected an implementation with a pre-1961 base-rate penalty inside F5; they are not an isolated test of the expectations hypothesis; the historical search stays closed because that result was seen and a redesign can now be aimed around it. B3, if sealed: bare E from THREEFYTP10 after the revision audit; no ratio, no literature sentence, no threshold. ACM may appear only as a dated second estimate in the audit note, not as a second live signal.

Q3. Changed. Do not keep C5 verbatim. The 0.18 pp gap is not “convention, not data”: at DTB3 4.04 the pinned BEY is 4.14 (0.10 convention); DGS3MO 4.22 leaves ~0.08 instrument/fitting. Say that, and say neither series may be substituted into the frozen logit (that substitution is ~3 pp of P: 14.8 → ~17.9). C6: strip 98% and Rosenberg–Maurer. A one-day KW share next to P is a counter-verdict. What may stand: model-dependent, revised, not an input.

Q4. C1–C4 ratified as in round 1, with the 5 bp freeze and the post-hoc disclosure in the same sentence. C4’s rule stays quarter-end + 32 + 10, labelled a heuristic, not a verified BEA vintage. C7 gate line changed: print “curve-only minus F5 = +3.89 pp, oracle-censored full path,” not “+27.1%”. The 198-origin interval does not sit under the §1.2 sentence unless the same episode-block interval (1000 draws, seed 42) is printed first for the 219-origin oracle-free path. 8.9% of draws ≤ 0 is a draw share, not a p-value.

Q5. Ledger string unchanged. Dashboard may prefix “Primary band rule:” and state that the paired supplement does not decide the verdict. Not “no robust signal.” The 12/198 fact stays off the verdict line.

AGREE: weights frozen until the 2027 refit; Part A converts both legs and does not splice GS3M; no B1/B2 run is authorized; ledger wording and the scoring key stay; C3 is ratified; C6 as committed (98% plus Rosenberg–Maurer beside P) does not stand.
DISAGREE: Gemini’s −0.50 pp automatic switch vs everyone else’s no-switch rule; C5 verbatim (DeepSeek, Opus) vs the 0.10/0.08 split (Fable, GPT, Kimi, me); C6 removed (Kimi) vs a bare decomposition (Fable, DeepSeek, me) vs Opus’s softened “almost all”; C7 interval under §1.2 (Opus, DeepSeek) vs oracle-free interval first (Gemini, Fable, me); “permanently closed like EBP” (Opus, Gemini) vs closed-search refusal without the §8.2 nickname (GPT).
CHANGED-MY-MIND: C5 is amended, not kept; daily conversion is mean-of-converted, with the convexity gap reported; the closure text must say E3 did not isolate the hypothesis; the C7 gate line prints +3.89 pp, not +27.1; the dashboard may name the band rule without a new verdict word.
message.reasoning:
I am Grok 4.7, preparing my council response.

I will attack two other councillors with specific rejected claims and mechanisms. I will steelman one missed idea from another councillor. I will revise my positions where warranted. I will end with the three required lists.

I am now reviewing my Round 1 positions and those of the other councillors to identify concrete attacks and a steelman. I will avoid filler, hedging, and compliments.

I have identified my first concrete attack. Gemini's non-inferiority switch to Curve_BEY is flawed because the discount convention is a nonlinear transformation of the three-month rate, not a constant bias. The gap is 0.10 percentage points at 4% and 0.81 at 15%, and four of twelve onsets fall in the high-rate window.

The −0.50 pp gate is a measurement correction in name only. Skill is computed on the same historical path that includes the four high-rate onsets. If BEY deepens those inversions by 0.3–0.8 pp, β and log-loss move together. The gate can therefore authorize an operational switch even when the skill gain is concentrated in the contaminated episodes. This selects a measurement on outcome and violates §1.3.

I verified the BEY formula is correct. The attack centers on the −0.50 pp automatic switch. Gemini himself flagged that the discount distortion may have been a helpful nonlinearity.

The −0.50 pp threshold is a decision rule tuned to a known bias direction. It is also numerically trivial: the oracle-free skill gain is only about 20 percentage points, so 0.50 pp is far below the signal and well inside noise.

The −0.50 pp threshold is a rubber stamp, not a non-inferiority test. The oracle-free skill gain is only about 0.002 nats. The censored set’s 90% bootstrap interval spans roughly 0.281 nats, so the standard error is about 0.085 nats. That 0.002 nat difference is just 0.03 standard deviations. The automatic switch therefore triggers in almost every case.

DeepSeek’s second attack targets C5. It demands keeping C5 verbatim while also calling the gap convention. Yet E1 and Fable show that at 4.04% the convention gap is only about 0.10 percentage points, leaving roughly 0.08 as instrument-specific. DeepSeek’s claim that the entire 0.18 is convention is factually wrong.

DeepSeek also turns Claude’s prediction threshold into a mandatory council trigger. Treating a prediction as a criterion is the same flaw as treating a wish as a rule.

I have identified a third attack on Claude Opus 5.5. Opus claims the standing warnings already cover the risk, so keeping a directional C6 is harmless. That reasoning treats an already breached firewall as justification for another breach. It is not a defense.

Opus also cites a prediction threshold of |Δβ| < 0.15. The current β is −1.2948 per percentage point of curve.

The 0.15 threshold for β is too low. A level-dependent gap of 0.5–0.8 percentage points on high-rate inversions can shift the regressor by a large fraction of typical inversion depth. The recent −1.57 percentage point inversion and deeper 1980s episodes mean β could easily move beyond 0.15 if those points are influential. I am now checking whether an increasing gap at high rates makes the discount curve less negative than the BEY curve.

The discount curve is always flatter than the BEY curve by the gap. At high three-month rates the gap reaches 0.55–0.81 percentage points, so the discount curve overstates curve level and understates inversion depth. Opus’s claim that the curve was overstated by 0.3–0.8 pp is therefore accurate. Fable’s observation that inversions were deeper than the model saw is consistent with this.

The |Δβ| < 0.15 threshold is unanchored. It equals roughly twelve percent of the current slope, yet the regressor error at the Volcker onsets is twenty to fifty percent of the inversion signal at those highest-leverage points. A bound of 0.15 therefore treats a wish as a hard limit.

Kimi’s Bonferroni override bar is a half-authorization. It offers a ready-made threshold for overriding the council while simultaneously claiming that confounding should not earn another shot. This is parking the second shot.

GPT’s points on 10,000 draws, the 5–95 interval, and proxy terminology are sound. GPT also correctly notes that F5 and curve-only labels reverse the attribution in C7.

GPT’s claim that F5 and curve-only labels reverse the attribution in C7 is wrong. The brief’s gate calculation shows F5 at 27.05 and curve-only at 23.16, so curve-only is higher by roughly 3.9 points. GPT’s C7 lists these figures as +23.2% versus +27.1%, which preserves that same direction. I will attack this misreading.

The real C7 problem is interval placement, not reversed attribution. Fable’s Jensen convexity point is the best missed idea: BEY of the mean daily spread differs from the mean of daily BEY values because the formula is convex in d.

I will adopt Fable’s mean-of-converted approach for the live path. I also need to correct C5: it wrongly claims the entire 0.18 gap is convention, but E1 and Fable show roughly 0.10 is convention and 0.08 is instrument-specific. I will amend C5 to reflect this.

I will adopt Fable’s verbatim disclaimer that E3’s −77.88 is not evidence against the hypothesis. This should be written into the draft even for a B3-only closure, so a future council cannot cite that number as a rejection of the economics.

The −77.88 figure is not a rejection of the hypothesis itself. It reflects a sealed test rejecting an implementation, and reopening is a second shot. Fable’s view that it is not evidence against the hypothesis is therefore correct. Both readings can be true: the implementation was rejected, but the underlying hypothesis was never isolated.

Gemini’s own risk paragraph undermines his switch rule. It shows the automatic trigger is more dangerous than he claimed.

Fable wants both KW and ACM in the context line. I will keep the bare number to avoid a directional nudge. I may adopt showing both estimates without ratios or literature.

I will attack Gemini’s −0.50 pp non-inferiority threshold and Opus’s |Δβ| < 0.15 bound as the two hardest targets, since both are interested parties. A brief hit on DeepSeek or GPT may follow. The Fable steelman is the mean-of-converted BEY formula plus the 0.10/0.08 convention-versus-instrument split, which requires amending C5.

Q1 will quantify the monthly-average bias for the mean-of-converted DTB3 formula. The automatic switch rule is rejected. Gemini’s −0.50 gate, DeepSeek’s 2 pp convening trigger, and Opus’s |Δβ| < 0.15 bound are all discarded as criteria. The decade table remains. GPT’s “91-day BEY proxy” label is adopted.

Q2 amends C5 by removing the false claim that the entire gap is convention. The split becomes roughly 0.10 convention and 0.08 instrument-specific. The anti-substitution sentence stays.

Q3 adds the E3 disclaimer to the closure text. It states that the sealed test rejected an implementation, not the isolated hypothesis, so historical retest remains closed.

Kimi objects to C7’s “F5 +23.2 % vs curve-only +27.1 %” wording because it prints +27.1 as a standalone figure, violating §1.2’s rule that the oracle-free +27.05 must never appear alone in public displays. A cleaner phrasing would be “curve-only exceeded F5 by 3.89 pp,” which avoids the standalone number while keeping the gate arithmetic intact.

The C7 gate will be rephrased as a difference: “curve-only minus F5 = +3.89 pp on the oracle-censored full path.” This removes the standalone +27.1 figure while keeping the arithmetic intact.

Q5 keeps the verdict string unchanged and places the methods sentence off the verdict line.

A dashboard prefix reading "Primary band rule:" can be added without changing the verdict token or ledger. This satisfies GPT and Kimi without accepting "no robust signal." Fable's claim that p ≈ 0.09 is rejected because the bootstrap share across nine blocks is not a calibrated p-value.

The AGREE list is now drafted. It covers converting both paths without the GS3M splice, keeping the automatic switch rule out, and closing B1/B2 permanently. The weights remain frozen until September 2027. C3 ratification and the unchanged ledger verdict string are also agreed.

C6’s 98% and R-M figures will be heavily cut or removed; Opus alone still wants the softened 98%. The five-basis-point disclosure is accepted as a post-hoc label only. No code will be written before the sealed specification.
